claims.paraphrase: Page title.
Page summary.
Table header row.
Three tiers hold Git content and manifests, D1 auth and opt-in tables, and R2 media bytes, each keyed as stated.
The selection rule column: what belongs in each tier.
Section heading.
Git is the source of truth for content.
Git is already the deploy trigger.
Git history serves as an audit trail at no extra infrastructure cost.
cairn stores no copy of an entry body outside git, only projections.
The content manifest holds one JSON row per entry with identity, routing, links, edges, tags, includes.
A save patches its manifest entry in the same commit as the content change.
The manifest lets admin and delivery answer graph questions without crawling GitHub.
Pointers to the content model and the media manifest section.
Section heading.
D1 holds what an admin request must look up in milliseconds, nothing from git history.
There are five tables across five migrations.
Each migration beyond the first is opt-in.
The baseline 0000 migration creates editor, magic_token, and session, present once AUTH_DB is wired.
A token and a session id are looked up by their SHA-256 hash.
0001_roles.sql drops the role CHECK so the app layer validates the declared vocabulary.
Pointer to the security model.
audit_log is opt-in, written only through createD1AuditSink, one row per audited action.
The audit timestamp is ISO 8601 because the column is read by people.
preview_tokens is opt-in, holds a hashed single-use token, and is swept on expiry without cron.
D1's role is narrow; a fact for git's audit trail goes in a commit.
Section heading.
A media block on the adapter gets an R2 bucket resolved at request time from the declared binding.
Each media manifest row carries display name, alt text, original filename, and pixel dimensions.
Delivery serves the stored MIME type verbatim.
The resolver returns the full-size path and adds a srcset ladder when transformations are on.
Diagram: an upload splits into R2 bytes and a git manifest row named by one hash prefix.
Bytes are addressed by content hash and the media manifest keyed by the 16-hex prefix is the dedup lookup.
R2 holds bytes because git and D1 do not suit large binaries; both manifests stay committed JSON.
Section heading.
Choose a tier by what must read the fact and how fast.
A site's extension data is unconstrained beyond the reserved cairn_ naming conventions.
Pointers to the two security model pages.
